title.narrative: CERF UFE for Response to Displacement and other priorities in Ethiopia (CERF-ETH-24-UF-1413)

description.narrative: Relief: The government-led returnee process has facilitated the movement of more than 150,000 internally displaced people from the Tigray and Amhara regions to contested Woredas in the southern and northwestern zones. These areas are already experiencing high levels of acute food insecurity, affecting many conflict-impacted individuals. Initial assessments by humanitarian partners indicate significant gaps in both food and non-food assistance, raising concerns of worsened humanitarian outcomes if these vulnerable households are not supported in a timely and adequate manner.The WFP and its partners have verified the returnees and provided food assistance during the initial months of their relocation to places of origin. However, significant funding gaps persist, jeopardizing the ability to deliver a predictable response to the food needs of the returnees. Currently, most returnees have limited access to income and food sources.Through other additional funding sources, WFP will provide monthly food rations to other verified returnees and extend assistance to an additional 80,000 severely food-insecure individuals from the local community who are already registered with the WFP. These households will receive pulses purchased with CERF funding, complemented by cereals and vegetable oil from other funding sources. To ensure an effective food response, the WFP will coordinate with partners and local authorities in returnee locations.UNHAS: UNHAS will provide humanitarian and development actors with access to air services, including regular and ad-hoc flights (e.g., for evacuations) in the Amhara region. Subject to needs, security assessments, and Government of Ethiopia (GoE) approvals, this may include helicopter support and/or the construction of an airstrip in Metema.If GoE approvals for helicopter support or airstrip construction in Metema are not granted within a reasonable timeframe, UNHAS will facilitate access to existing regional airports for regular use or ad-hoc cases (e.g., medical or security evacuations), especially if Ethiopian Airlines halts operations in parts of the region.This funding may also be allocated to support UNHAS operations across the country, addressing the limited funding available this year.Logistics Cluster: The Logistics Cluster facilitates access to common logistics services, sectoral coordination, and information management to address identified logistical challenges. In the Amhara region, the cluster supports partners facing difficulties in transporting and storing humanitarian cargo, particularly as security in the region continues to deteriorate. This support serves as a last resort for enabling humanitarian responses.
